title.narrative: UNFPA - stöd till landprogram i DRK

description.narrative:
Denna insats syftar till att förstärka UNFPA: s kapacitet att leverera de resultat som anges i organisationens landprogram för Demokratiska Republiken Kongo under perioden 2020-2023.
I DRK är alla indikatorer som rör kvinnors hälsa, sexuella och reproduktiva tjänster och rättigheter (SRHR) oroande, framförallt är den knappa tillgången till preventivmedel och det höga antalet ungdomsgraviditeter alarmerande. Dessutom är den övergripande policymiljön när det gäller SRHR och befolkningsdynamik inte anpassad till landets utmaningar. UNFPA är en nyckelaktör i DRK, vars starka insatser inom ramen för dess globala mandat behövs för att stödja både beslutsfattare, genomförande aktörer på internationell och nationell nivå, och kunna nå ut till olika målgrupper som kvinnor, ungdomar, vårdgivare och institutioner.
Detta institutionella stöd till UNFPA ger dem flexibilitet, frihet och medel för att positionera sig och ge stöd till aktörer inom SRHR och relaterade frågor i landet.

This contribution aims at strenthening UNFPA's capacity to deliver on the results set by the organisation's country programme for DRC covering the period 2020-2023.
In DRC, all indicators concerning maternal health, sexual and reproductive services and rights (SRHR), including poor access to contraceptives are alarming. Also, overall policy environment with regards to SRHR and population dynamics is inadapted to country's challenges. UNFPA is a key actor in DRC whose strong action within the framework of its global mandate is needed to support both decision makers, implementing actors (international and national), and different target groups (professionals as well as services users, such as the youth).
This contribution proposes providing an institutional support to UNFPA in the country to allow them flexibility, freedom and means to position themselves and provide the needed assistance to the multitude of actors on SRHR and related issues in the country.

This contribution is intended to support the UNFPA DRC country office in contributing to the following objectives: (1) strengthened national capacities to improve financing and develop and implement policies and programmes that address sexual and reproductive health and right’s needs; (2) integrated high quality services delivery and information for maternal health, family planning, Sexually Transmitted Infections/HIV, (3) to ensure that young people and adolescents, especially disadvantaged adolescent’s girls are empowered to have the capacity to claim their rights and access to sexual and reproductive health services; (4) to strengthened national accountability mechanisms to prevent SGBV and promote gender equality and to provide holistic care to victims of SGBV. These objectives will be pursued in stable as well as in humanitarian context.
In addition to the aformentioned objectives it has been decided to provide additional support to UNFPA, as the global champion on Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and as the lead agency of the Task Force on SEA allegations in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), to strengthen safeguarding mechanisms including prevention, response, coordination and community engagement with regards to PSEA.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
A new senior acting Country Representative arrived in 2023, who managed to push donor engagement and UNFPAs visibility. Engagement with the Embassy increased during this period. Following DRCs pilot to roll out Universal Health Care (UHC) in Kinshasa, by providing free maternal health care in certain health zones, UNFPA launched a "forum of women leaders on maternal and neonatal health", which was led by the first lady. The forum managed to organise national dialogues and field visits with engagement and support from different ministers, donors, civil society, UN, INGOs and private sector, and several commitments (at different levels) were made. The Embassy partook in the panel discussion on one of the national dialogues, where we reiterated our commitment and support to organisations working on SRHR and maternal health in the country. Other donors (Canada, EU, Norway) did the same. The forum allowed the GIBS (Donor Coordination Group for Health) to also reiterate their commitments and remind governmental partners of the challenges the country faces with regards to maternal health that requires attention at the highest level, beyond the Ministry of Health and national committee for UHC. A report and roadmap are to be developed from the forum events. Following the forum events, the GIBS highlighted some main points that should be prioritisied and followed up on: 1) Resolving the systemic and structural problem of human resources for health, in terms of numbers, capacity building, motivation, ethics and career management 2) Funding of multisectoral interventions that impact on the wellbeing and development of women through the decentralised territorial entities (ETD) 3) Strengthening the governance and protocol of GIBS and GCP to improve the effective coordination of the development support provided by donors.
With regards to the evaluation of the 5th Country Programme (20202024), the Embassy was invited to be part of a reference group, consisting of government entities, academia, NGO partners to UNFPA, donors among others, who will support and quality assure the evaluation. The Embassy participated in the startup meeting organised by UNFPA to look at the ToRs for the evaluation. The ToR are well structured and aligns with UNFPAs strategic plan (20222025), there were only few things that was highlighted to the consultant during the meeting: - There need to also look at UNFPAs humanitarian and coordination work (where challenge has been on which activities can be deemed as "life saving"), - There is no baseline for Family Planning, which should be added. - Increase indicators related to midwifery, especially since the law regarding the midwifery profession came about. - Need to improve GBV indicators. The Embassy stressed an additional two points that were considered for the evaluation: 1) The inclusion of People Living with Disabilities (PLWD) 2) UNFPAs coordination role within UNCT and HCT, where UNFPA has played an important role in improving and increasing SRHR and GBV interventions across. Complementarities between both regional and global strategies were noticed during 2023. With funding from Sida's Regional SRHR Team under the 2gether 4SRHR programme, UNFPA DRC was among the leading countries to finalise their readiness assessment on DRCs implementation of the MISP for SRHR in emergency settings. The assessment highlighted many challenges that need to be addressed in order for MISP to be implemented. Among the challenges were lack of funds to support health and/or SRHR emergency preparedness at national or subnational level, insufficient supplies and equipment, integration of emergency SRH or MISP in policy and strategic documents. UNFPA Country Office developed an action plan based on these recommendations. As a result of the MISP assessment, the Embassy decided to place a greater emphasis on advocating for SRHR in emergencies, which is supporting UNFPAs efforts on implementing MISP for SRHR in emergencies. There has been vague interest to support and finance SRHR in emergencies, as it has not been deemed life saving in humanitarian terms. The Embassy therefore decided to lift this as a dialogue topic and advocacy topic. In June, the Embassy secured a presentation slot for UNFPA to present MISP and their action plan. The Embassy also organised an event on SRHR in humanitarian settings, where organisations such as Ipas and UNFPA presented the need to include SRHR in humanitarian settings and to finance these interventions.
Another complementarity was seen with regards to Maternal Health, where Sida HQ supports the UNFPA Maternal Health Trust Fund (MHTF), of which DRC is an eligible country because of the high rates of maternal deaths. The support to MHTF is coming to an end, but a new support is being prepared for MHTF (20242026), where the Embassy has been asked to provide input from a country perspective. In preparation for a new MHTF support and to support the achievement of results in the DRC, the Embassy has urged UNFPA and Sida HQ to assess how the integration between SRHR and Maternal Health can be strengthened and to have a nexus perspective in the appraisal. The above has strengthened collaboration with Sida colleagues at HQ with the ambition to ensure synergies and maximum impact of the bilateral and global support to UNFPA. These exchanges are useful as the Embassy is in a position to also follow up on global support that trickles down to DRC.
Sweden provided funding for UNFPAs PSEA work which financed 4 field coordinators. After 2022, UNFPA asked for continued funding for the coordinators, but the Embassy was not in a position to continue funding this despite PSEA being a priority question for the Embassy. Seeing the importance of the PSEA work UNFPA is doing, the Country Office decided to continue funding this through their core resources. In June 2023, the Embassy did a field trip to North Kivu and Ituri to assess UNFPAs PSEA (and GBV) work and the results of the Swedish funding to PSEA. It was impressive to see the capacity UNFPA has built in PSEA and PSEA coordination, this includes the capacity of the PSEA coordinators that Sweden supported. UNFPA plays a key role in different steering and technical committees. The coordinators led the PSEA network (a network consisting of organisations who operate in humanitarian settings) and UNFPA (as co-financers) also support the PSEA coordinator at the Humanitarian Coordinators Office. The coordination with other UN agencies in the field works very well. UNFPA works closely with OCHA and the peace keeping mission on CBCM and the monitoring of these. UNFPA in Bunia was responsible for sensitising humanitarian actors and communities. Following the visit to North Kivu and Ituri it became clearer that UNFPA is now playing the role of a double mandated organisation. They are working hard to access more humanitarian funding to respond to SRHR/GBV in humanitarian settings.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
